page: Hetzner Cloud ccx53 is a dedicated CPU server powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes a 32 MB L3 cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. The system is equipped with 125.0 GB of RAM, yielding approximately 3.91 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a 600 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance runs under a QEMU hypervisor. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results show strong performance in several areas, particularly in single-core CPU stress tests, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core metrics, which all rank in the top 25%. Image and text processing, along with CPU encryption tests, also demonstrate strong capabilities. Memory performance is notable, with a PassMark memory score in the top 25%, though uncached read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into the average range at 84.57 GB/sec and 62.84 GB/sec respectively. Large-scale LLM text generation using a 70B model is a weak point, scoring in the bottom 10%, whereas text generation with a small 135M model reaches top-tier speeds.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ccx53 offers a balanced resource density suitable for production workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources without the premium of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The combination of 32 dedicated vCPUs, a 600 GB NVMe SSD, and 125.0 GB of RAM makes this server well-suited for general-purpose applications, multi-threaded software compilation, medium-scale database operations, text and image processing pipelines, and web serving.
description: Hetzner Cloud ccx53 is a dedicated CPU server featuring 32 vCPUs (16 physical cores, 2 threads per core) powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. It is configured with 125.0 GB of RAM (3.91 GB per core) and 600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage under a QEMU hypervisor. Benchmarks indicate strong performance in single-core CPU tasks, multi-core Geekbench tests, and encryption, placing them in the top 25% of tested systems. While large-scale LLM text generation is weak, the server delivers solid average performance for database operations, web serving, and software compilation. This balanced resource profile offers a cost-effective solution for dedicated compute needs. It is highly suitable for general-purpose workloads, image and text processing, and medium-scale database deployments.
